pill.desc: amethyst, opaque, hard gelatin capsule with yellow radial bars on the cap

tell: Autoinhibition of its own CYP2C19 clearance and a magnesium trihydrate salt mark the single-enantiomer successor to omeprazole.

clues.text: Systemic bioavailability rises from about 64% after one dose to about 90% at steady state, because the drug inhibits its own CYP2C19 clearance. It is 97% bound to plasma proteins.
A magnesium salt, the trihydrate weighing 767.2 against 345.4 for the free active moiety. It is only slightly soluble in water.
Approved under an NDA in 20 mg and 40 mg strengths, with granule packets from 2.5 to 40 mg. Dosed once daily.
No boxed warning; contraindicated with rilpivirine-containing products and in hypersensitivity to the drug or its chemical relatives. Headache and diarrhea are the most frequent adverse reactions.
Short-term healing of erosive esophagitis and its maintenance, relief of heartburn from reflux disease, reducing NSAID-associated gastric ulcer risk, and H. pylori eradication with antibiotics.
Blocks the final step of acid production by inhibiting the H⁺/K⁺ ATPase of gastric parietal cells, after conversion to an active sulphenamide in their acidic compartment.
The generic name begins with E and has twelve letters.
